content.text: Zimbabwean digital creators, you know the pain of relying on platforms that can freeze your funds, shut your store, or even reject your payments. You've tried using Stripe or PayPal, but they've locked you out or refused to let you sell your digital products due to local restrictions. It's time to break free from this cycle of dependence and take control of your commerce infrastructure. By deploying a sovereign digital commerce stack, you can be your own payment processor, file delivery system, and order database, all while keeping your customer data and revenue safe from interference. In this article, we'll explore how Supabase can be the backbone of your digital store's order database, and walk you through the process of setting up a reliable and scalable commerce infrastructure.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

Platforms like Stripe and PayPal may have failed you, but that's exactly why you need your own sovereign commerce infrastructure. By hosting your store on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, you can process payments with NOWPayments, deliver files with Google Drive or Cloudflare R2, and store orders with Supabase. This decentralized approach means you're not dependent on any single platform or payment processor, making it impossible for them to shut you down or freeze your funds. With Supabase as your order database, you can rest assured that your customer data and orders are safe and accessible, even if the platform you're using decides to restrict your access or shut down your store.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before you can deploy your sovereign commerce stack, you'll need to sign up for a few free services: GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and Supabase for your order database. You'll also need to set up a NOWPayments account to process payments. Don't worry, these services are all free and will get you up and running in no time. Once you've signed up, you can start building your stack and deploying it to the cloud.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you'll need to configure NOWPayments to work with your Supabase order database. This involves setting up a webhook to trigger when a payment is processed, and then using that webhook to update your Supabase database with the new order. You'll also need to set up Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 to deliver files to your customers. Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once you've set up your payment and delivery pipeline, it's time to go live and process your first transaction. This involves deploying your stack to the cloud, configuring the necessary services, and testing everything to make sure it's working as expected. With Supabase as your order database, you can rest assured that your customer data and orders are safe and accessible, even if the platform you're using decides to restrict your access or shut down your store. To get started, simply deploy your stack to the cloud and test everything to make sure it's working as expected.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Once your infrastructure is running smoothly, it's time to start scaling. This involves setting up load balancing, caching, and other performance optimizations to ensure that your store can handle a large volume of traffic. With Supabase as your order database, you can rest assured that your customer data and orders are safe and accessible, even as your store grows and becomes more successful. How do I build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free?

The setup sequence matters because each component depends on the previous one being correctly configured. Start with NOWPayments: create your account, configure wallet addresses for each coin you want to accept, generate the API key, and note the IPN secret key you will set. Then configure the backend: in Stack 01, deploy the Google Apps Script Web App and note its URL; in Stack 02, deploy the Cloudflare Worker and note its URL. Set that URL as the webhook endpoint in your NOWPayments IPN settings. Then configure the storefront: Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages with your product pages and checkout flow pointing to the backend. Then run a real mainnet test — send actual crypto to your configured wallet address, confirm NOWPayments detects it, confirm the webhook fires to your backend, confirm the order appears in your database, and confirm the delivery email arrives with a working download link. Only after the complete pipeline test passes should you make the store URL public. COREMERCH runs this complete test before handoff on every deployment.
Test a real mainnet transaction before you promote — finding a configuration error with your own crypto costs less than finding it with a buyer's.

Your Deployment Checklist

Here's a checklist of the steps you need to take to deploy your sovereign commerce stack with Supabase as your order database:  * Sign up for a GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages account for hosting * Set up a Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script account for backend logic * Create a Supabase account for your order database * Set up a NOWPayments account to process payments * Configure NOWPayments to work with your Supabase order database * Set up Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 to deliver files to your customers * Deploy your stack to the cloud and test everything to make sure it's working as expected  Once you've completed these steps, you'll be ready to go live and start processing transactions with your sovereign commerce stack.
Follow the setup sequence in order: backend first, payment layer second, mainnet test third, promote fourth.
